Cyber Attack Disrupts Russian Hospitality Firms as Ransomware Hits Operations

A major cyber attack has disrupted operations across Russia’s hospitality industry, with several hotel chains and independent operators reporting ransomware incidents affecting booking and property management systems. The attack, which began late Thursday, is ongoing, leaving staff and guests facing significant challenges.

The National Hospitality Association reported that at least 35 hotels in Moscow, St. Petersburg, and Sochi have been impacted, including properties managed by the Dvorets Group and Volna Hospitality Services. “Guest check-ins are being done manually, and we’re unable to process electronic payments or access reservation data,” said Irina Lebedeva, spokesperson for the Dvorets Group, which operates 11 properties in western Russia.

Industry insiders say the attack has forced many firms to temporarily suspend online reservations, with some hotels unable to access guest records or room allocation systems. Staff are working overtime to manage check-ins and respond to guest complaints. “The front desk teams are under immense pressure,” said Yelena Markova, a union representative for hotel workers in St. Petersburg. “Employees are working long hours to ensure guests receive essential services despite the IT breakdown.”

Trade analysts estimate that daily losses for the sector may exceed 200 million rubles as a result of cancelled bookings and operational disruptions. The Russian Hospitality Chamber urged firms to bolster cyber defenses and called on authorities for technical assistance. “This event highlights the urgent need for stronger digital infrastructure in the hospitality sector,” said Chamber Chairperson Viktor Petrov.

Officials have not indicated when normal operations might resume, as technical teams continue to assess the scope of the attack.
